c.pop: ~1.5 million (Zhangjiajie prefecture-level city, spanning Yongding District, Wulingyuan District, Cili County and Sangzhi County)
c.tagline: Where the sandstone pillars of Avatar's Pandora rise straight out of the mist

card: Cash and mobile QR payments (Alipay, WeChat Pay) dominate almost every transaction, from noodle stalls to scenic-area ticket booths; foreign Visa/Mastercard are accepted only at large international hotels like the InterContinental or Pullman. Set up Alipay's Tour Pass or link a foreign card to WeChat Pay before arrival, and carry some cash as backup.

taxi.fareNote: About ¥1.8–2/km after the first 2–3 km; drivers rarely speak English so have your destination written in Chinese characters or use Didi's in-app translation

emergency.note: Fire is 119. Tourist police booths are stationed at the entrances of Zhangjiajie National Forest Park and Tianmen Mountain; hotel front desks are often the fastest way to get help translated.

religion: Tujia and Miao ethnic folk traditions
walk: Not a stroll-around city — Zhangjiajie is a hiking and cable-car destination built into vertical sandstone-pillar terrain. Expect thousands of stone steps, steep switchback trails, and long walkways through the national forest park; shuttle buses, cable cars, and the Bailong Elevator handle the big elevation changes. Downtown Yongding District is flat and walkable.

safety.safety: Very safe for solo travelers by international standards; violent crime against tourists is extremely rare. The main risks are trail-related — steep drop-offs, slick stone steps in rain or fog, and getting lost off marked paths.
safety.crime: Petty theft is uncommon but not unheard of at peak-season entrances; standard vigilance with valuables is enough. Overcharging by unlicensed tour touts and off-app taxi drivers is the more common annoyance.

hood_landmark.Yongding District (Downtown Zhangjiajie): Tianmen Mountain cable car base station
hood_landmark.Wulingyuan District: Zhangjiajie National Forest Park & Golden Whip Stream

avoid.reason: Ignore unlicensed taxis and aggressive tour touts at the train station and park gates, and expect crushing queues at the Bailong Elevator on holidays.

hood_desc: The prefecture's urban core, with the train and long-distance bus stations, the bulk of mid-range hotels, restaurants, and the world's longest cable car line climbing straight out of the city to Tianmen Mountain.
The gateway town to the core UNESCO scenic area, packed with guesthouses just outside the National Forest Park gate; this is the launch point for Golden Whip Stream and the Bailong Elevator.
A quieter valley within Wulingyuan Scenic Area centered on Baofeng Lake's jade-green water and the pillar-lined Ten-Mile Gallery, popular for an easier-paced day away from the busiest trails.
Home to the park's most photographed pillar formations, including the cliffs said to have inspired the floating Hallelujah Mountains of Pandora in Avatar.
An adventure-tourism hub built around the record-breaking glass bridge spanning the Zhangjiajie Grand Canyon, with zip-lining and bungee add-ons for thrill-seekers.

water.note: Drink bottled or boiled water; tap water is not potable.

transit.sys: No metro or tram; city buses run downtown, and mandatory eco-friendly shuttle buses (fare included in the park ticket) move visitors between trailheads inside Zhangjiajie National Forest Park and Wulingyuan Scenic Area.
transit.hours: City buses roughly 6:30am–7pm; park shuttles run from park opening (~7am) to around 6pm, earlier in winter
transit.pay: Cash, Alipay, or WeChat Pay on city buses; scenic-area shuttles are covered by your entrance ticket
transit.map: Amap (Gaode Ditu) or Baidu Maps for navigation; free paper trail maps handed out at park entrance gates
transit.note: Cable cars, the Bailong Elevator, and the Tianmen Mountain cable car all require separate paid tickets on top of park admission.

transport.air: Zhangjiajie Hehua International Airport (DYG) has direct flights from Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, Chengdu, Xi'an, and other major Chinese hubs, plus seasonal charters from a handful of Southeast Asian cities.
transport.train: Zhangjiajie West high-speed rail station puts Changsha about 2 hours away and links onward to the national high-speed network; the older Zhangjiajie railway station handles slower conventional trains.
transport.bus: Long-distance coaches connect Zhangjiajie's bus stations to Changsha, Fenghuang Ancient Town, and other Hunan destinations.
transport.ferry: None — Zhangjiajie is deep inland in mountainous northwestern Hunan with no navigable ferry routes.
transport.car: Self-driving is possible via the Changsha–Zhangjiajie and Zhangjiajie–Jishou expressways, but requires a Chinese driving permit; mountain roads within the scenic areas are best left to shuttle buses or a hired driver.

airport.name: Zhangjiajie Hehua International Airport
airport.distance: ~7 miles (11 km) south of downtown Zhangjiajie (Yongding District)
airport.transport: Taxi ~$8–12 (20–25 min); airport shuttle bus to city center for around $1.50; no direct rail link

net.m: China Mobile, China Unicom, and China Telecom all sell prepaid tourist SIMs with data at the airport and downtown shops; eSIM options from international providers also work well
net.w: Free Wi-Fi is common in hotels and many cafes downtown, but weaker to nonexistent deep inside the scenic parks
net.ops: China Mobile, China Unicom, China Telecom
net.gb: $3–6 per GB on a prepaid tourist SIM
net.fwn: Google, Gmail, Maps, Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, and most Western news sites are blocked; install a reliable VPN before you arrive
net.ap: Cell signal is generally solid even on cable cars and ridgelines, though it can drop in valley trails and cave sections like Tianmen Cave

tip.s: Tipping is not customary anywhere in China, including for taxi drivers, hotel staff, or tour guides; attempting to tip can even cause confusion.
tip.r: Restaurants do not expect tips and never add a service charge at local eateries; only some high-end international hotel restaurants may quietly include one.

food.name: Sanxiaguo
food.desc: Three things thrown in one pot: cured pork, tripe and pig cheek simmered with radish, potato and tofu skin. Choose the dry pot or the milder soup pot.

places.name: Hu Shifu Sanxia Guo
places.note: One of the best-known sanxiaguo houses in town; huge portions and intense smoked-meat flavor.

places.name: Ye Hua Xiang
places.note: Comfortable room, consistent local cooking, around 60-80 CNY a head. A good first stop.

places.name: Le Kou Fu Homestyle Restaurant
places.note: Opposite the city hospital; built its name on carefully made traditional Zhangjiajie food.

food.name: Tujia Dry Pot
food.desc: Gan guo: chicken, beef or river fish stir-fried with dried chilies and Sichuan pepper, then kept bubbling over a burner while you add vegetables.

places.name: Ye Hua Xiang
places.note: Reliable dry pots with adjustable heat; ask for wei la if you want it toned down.

places.name: Sanjiaoping small restaurants
places.note: No-frills local block where residents eat; the cheapest authentic pots in the city.

places.name: Ziwu Road eateries
places.note: Another local strip of family kitchens, busy at dinner and rarely touristed.

food.name: Tujia Cured Smoked Pork
food.desc: Larou: pork hung over a wood fire through the winter until dark and intensely savory, then sliced thin and stir-fried with garlic shoots or bamboo.

places.name: Ye Hua Xiang
places.note: Smoked meats are its strongest suit; a good introduction to Tujia mountain cooking.

places.name: Le Kou Fu Homestyle Restaurant
places.note: Home-style stir-fries of larou with seasonal mountain vegetables.

places.name: Wulingyuan village restaurants
places.note: Farmhouse kitchens near the park gate that cure their own pork; handy after a day hiking.

food.name: Xiangxi Sour Fish Soup
food.desc: Western Hunan sour cooking: river fish simmered in a broth soured with fermented tomato and pickled chili, aromatic rather than simply hot.

places.name: Le Kou Fu Homestyle Restaurant
places.note: Does the Xiangxi sour and pickled-chili dishes with a lighter hand than most.

places.name: Sanjiaoping restaurants
places.note: Local block where sour fish and pickled vegetable dishes are everyday food.

food.name: Tujia Ciba and Hezha
food.desc: Ciba are glutinous rice cakes pounded by hand and toasted over coals; hezha is a thick soup of ground soybean and wild greens. Classic Tujia village food.

places.name: Xibu Street food stalls
places.note: Tujia-themed pedestrian street with ciba pounded and grilled in front of you.

places.name: Wulingyuan village stalls
places.note: Roadside stands near the park gates selling ciba hot off the grill for a few yuan.

food.name: Zhangjiajie Rice Noodles
food.desc: The standard local breakfast: soft rice noodles in bone broth topped with stewed beef or pork ribs, chili oil and pickled greens. Eaten before dawn hikes.

places.name: Sanjiaoping noodle shops
places.note: Open from early morning; where locals eat before work, cheap and fast.

places.name: Ziwu Road noodle shops
places.note: Another cluster of morning noodle counters, most closed by mid-morning.

food.name: Tujia Rice Wine
food.desc: Mijiu: cloudy homemade glutinous rice wine, sweet and low in alcohol, poured from jars at family restaurants. Often warmed in the cold months.

places.name: Ye Hua Xiang
places.note: Serves house rice wine by the jug as the traditional partner to sanxiaguo.

places.name: Wulingyuan farmhouse restaurants
places.note: Village kitchens brew their own; usually the freshest and cheapest you will find.

food.name: Tujia Oil Tea Soup
food.desc: You cha tang: tea leaves fried in oil with ginger and puffed rice or peanuts, then poured hot. Savory and warming, drunk as a snack rather than a beverage.

places.name: Xibu Street teahouses
places.note: Tujia-themed street where oil tea comes with rice-cracker toppings, often with live music.

places.name: Tujia village homestays
places.note: The traditional setting; many homestays offer it to arriving guests.

landmarks: Zhangjiajie National Forest Park
Three thousand quartzite pillars drift in and out of mist in China's first national forest park, the landscape that inspired Avatar's Pandora.
Yuanjiajie & Hallelujah Mountain
Home of the Southern Sky Column—officially renamed 'Avatar Hallelujah Mountain'—and the natural stone arch called First Bridge Under Heaven.
Tianmen Mountain
One of the world's longest cableways climbs to Heaven's Gate, a 131-meter natural arch reached by 999 steps and vertiginous glass skywalks.
Zhangjiajie Grand Canyon Glass Bridge
Walk 300 meters above the canyon floor on the world-famous glass-bottomed suspension bridge, then descend past waterfalls into the gorge below.
Bailong Elevator
A 326-meter glass elevator bolted to a sheer cliff face rockets sightseers skyward—the world's tallest outdoor lift.
Tianzi Mountain
The 'Son of Heaven' peaks serve the park's most celebrated sea-of-clouds sunrises above ranks of needle-thin sandstone towers.
Golden Whip Stream
A gentle 7.5-kilometer valley walk beneath towering pillars, where wild macaques patrol crystal waters—Zhangjiajie's loveliest low-level trail.
Yellow Dragon Cave (Huanglongdong)
A vast show cave of underground rivers and the 19.2-meter 'Sea-Suppressing Needle' stalagmite, famously insured for a billion yuan.
Baofeng Lake
An emerald mountain lake cupped by karst peaks, toured by boat while local Tujia singers serenade from the wooded shores.
Ten-Mile Natural Gallery
A miniature tram trundles up a valley lined with named peaks like the Three Sisters, a painterly corridor of pinnacles.

train.note: There are no international trains anywhere near Zhangjiajie. Zhangjiajie West station, opened in December 2019 on the Qianjiang-Changde high-speed line, cuts Changsha to about three hours but lies outside the city; the original Zhangjiajie station on the Jiaozuo-Liuzhou railway takes the conventional services, including roughly four hours to Changsha and Huaihua and an overnight train up from Shenzhen West. Book on 12306 with your passport - the window opens 15 days ahead, and summer and the October holiday sell out fast because this is one of China's busiest domestic tourist destinations. Both stations are some way from Wulingyuan, the park entrance village, so factor in a further bus or taxi.

bus.note: No international buses serve Zhangjiajie. Intercity coaches from Changsha's West bus terminal run roughly hourly until about 19:00, take about five hours and cost around ¥120; there are also useful direct buses to Fenghuang ancient town (about four hours) that no train covers. The Central Bus Station sits next to Zhangjiajie railway station, and frequent local buses shuttle between the city, Wulingyuan and the park gates. Tickets are sold at the counter; bring your passport.

ferry.note: Zhangjiajie is deep inland in the mountains of northwestern Hunan with no navigable river route in or out, so there are no passenger ferries. The boat trips on Baofeng Lake and the Mengdong River are scenic-area attractions rather than a way of reaching the city.

half.name: Mengdong River
half.blurb: Narrow river gorge where rafts drift past forested cliffs and small rapids outside the national park.

full.name: Fenghuang Ancient Town
full.blurb: Riverside old town of wooden stilt houses and stone bridges along the Tuo River, home to Miao and Tujia communities.

full.name: Furong (Hibiscus) Town
full.blurb: Cliffside old town built around a waterfall that drops through the middle of its stone streets.
